text: The patient failed six weeks of documented conservative therapy including NSAIDs and physical therapy before MRI was ordered. The attached notes show progressive neurological deficit, which meets the plan's published criteria for advanced imaging. Overturned on first-level appeal after peer-to-peer.

A same-specialty peer reviewer was requested. The treating physician's letter tied each criterion in the payer's clinical policy to a dated chart entry. The denial was reversed because the criteria were met on the face of the record.

Documented contraindication to the first-line alternative (renal impairment) with lab values attached. The reviewer accepted that the less intensive option was clinically inappropriate and approved the service.

The procedure note documented a separate anatomical site and a separate indication from the primary procedure. Modifier 59 was supported by the operative report, and the NCCI edit was overridden on appeal.
Two sessions on the same date, with a documented break between them and different diagnoses. Time stamps from the record were attached, and the payer reprocessed with the distinct-service modifier.

The service was urgent and performed after hours; the authorization line was requested the next business morning and the request log was attached. The payer granted retrospective authorization and paid the claim.
An authorization number existed but was keyed to the wrong CPT. The approved authorization letter was attached showing the intended service, and the claim was corrected and paid.

The clearinghouse 277CA acceptance report showed the original submission well inside the filing limit. Attaching that dated report and the contract filing-limit page led the payer to reverse the denial.
A prior rejection letter dated inside the limit proved an earlier submission with a correctable error. The payer treated the corrected claim as timely.
The RARC indicated a missing rendering provider NPI. A corrected claim with frequency code 7 was submitted with the original remittance attached and paid within the normal cycle.
The claim was missing the referring provider. The referral record was attached with a corrected claim, and it was reprocessed without further dispute.
Modifier 25 was missing on the E/M billed the same day as a minor procedure. The note documented a significant, separately identifiable evaluation. The corrected claim was paid in full.
The diagnosis pointer referenced a non-specific code. The note supported a more specific ICD-10 code that is on the payer's covered list. A corrected claim was reprocessed and paid.

The member's plan language covered the service when performed for the documented condition. A written request for the exact exclusion relied upon was never answered with a specific provision, and the denial was reversed.
Each additional visit was tied to a documented change in clinical status with updated orders. The payer approved the units on review.
The requested records were sent inside the request window with the attachment control number on the cover sheet. The claim was reprocessed and paid.
Eligibility printout showed active coverage on the date of service. The payer corrected its own member match and reprocessed the claim.
The earlier claim was for a different date of service with a transposed digit. A copy of both claims showing the distinct dates led to reversal.
